properties.state: {"description":"The loop hook stops merely COUNTING writes and starts recognising SHAPES, so a skill is named when the situation calling for it arrives rather than when the agent happens to remember: a file edit with no ChangeEvent means impact-check; a change recorded but never PROPAGATED also means impact-check (BL-163); a recorded change with no artifact link means link-artifacts; a capture batch with no gap pass means detect-and-ask; a rendering written and nothing stored means session-artifacts. Extends `req:nudge-covers-bypass`, which already arms on file-edit events and already names those skills — what was missing was the pattern, not the trigger. This is the half of BL-74 the existing rungs structurally cannot reach: they compute loop debt from graph state, and these situations are invisible to the graph. BL-163 CORRECTED THE FIRST SHAPE AND ADDED THE ONE ARMING BRANCH THIS CAPABILITY HAS. As shipped, impact-check keyed on `changes == 0` — it fired only when a session recorded NOTHING — so a session that edited code and wrote its ChangeEvents up AFTERWARDS had `changes > 0` and was met with silence, while every one of those events was the bookkeeping-after the hook's own message says is not the loop. It measured a ChangeEvent's PRESENCE where it meant its PRECEDENCE, and the root cause was that `CHANGE_OPS` held only RECORDING ops while no set counted `propagate_change` or `propagate_from` at all: the hook could not separate recording from looking because it never counted looking. Every other shape refines a nudge already firing and adds no interruption; this one had to ARM, because the session it catches has no unchecked writes and has touched reflow2, so there was no nudge for a shape to refine.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"The moment tells the agent which skill it needs","provenance":"authored","status":"verified","tier":"operational"}
